tests.procedure: Under strong white light, check each received sample container separately in a clean transparent watch glass or glass dish for foreign particles, colour and compliance with the visual specification.

details.vessel: clean, transparent watch glass or glass dish
details.reference: BP 2024 Monograph for Sodium Lauryl Sulfate

tests.procedure: Stepwise solubility determination with the solvent (water, ethanol 96 per cent) at 25.0 +/- 0.5 C: shake 1 min and hold 15 min at temperature between each addition; classify by the volume needed to dissolve 100 mg.

details.shakeEachStep: vigorously, 1 min, then 15 min in constant temperature; if not dissolved repeat shaking 1 min and 15 min
steps: 100 mg in stoppered tube + 0.1 mL solvent: dissolved = very soluble
add further 0.9 mL solvent (total 1 mL): dissolved = freely soluble
add further 2 mL (total 3 mL): dissolved = soluble
add further 7 mL (total 10 mL): dissolved = sparingly soluble
not dissolved: 10 mg powdered substance + 10 mL solvent: dissolved = slightly soluble
not dissolved: 1 mg powdered substance + 10 mL solvent: dissolved = very slightly soluble
details.reference: BP 2023 Monograph for Sodium Lauryl Sulfate

tests.procedure: Mix the sample intimately with potassium bromide and compress into a transparent pellet. Examine the IR spectrum and compare with the spectrum of Sodium lauryl Sulfate RS.

details.reference: BP 2024 Appendix II A. Infrared Spectrophotometry; BP 2023 Monograph for Sodium Lauryl Sulfate

tests.procedure: Place 2.5 g in a silica or platinum crucible, add 2 mL of 500 g/L sulfuric acid, heat on a water-bath then progressively over an open flame, ignite in a muffle furnace at 600 +/- 25 C until black particles have disappeared; cool; add a few drops of 100 g/L sulfuric acid, heat and ignite as above; add a few drops of ammonium carbonate solution, evaporate to dryness, ignite as above, cool. Dissolve the residue in 50 mL water and mix. To 2 mL of this solution add 4 mL potassium pyroantimonate solution R1 (rub the inside of the test tube with a glass rod if necessary).

details.ammoniumCarbonateSolution: a few drops, evaporate to dryness
details.testPortion: 2 mL of the solution + 4 mL potassium pyroantimonate solution R1
details.expected: A white, crystalline precipitate is formed
details.reference: BP 2023 Monograph for Sodium Lauryl Sulfate

tests.procedure: Dissolve 10 g in 100 mL water. After acidification with hydrochloric acid, boil for 20 min; no precipitate is formed. Add 120 g/L barium chloride solution; a white precipitate is produced.

details.reagent: 120 g/L solution of barium chloride R (volume not stated)
details.reference: BP 2023 Monograph for Sodium Lauryl Sulfate

tests.procedure: Dissolve 0.1 g in 10 mL of water and shake.

details.reference: BP 2023 Monograph for Sodium Lauryl Sulfate

tests.procedure: Dissolve 1.0 g in 100 mL carbon dioxide-free water, add 0.1 mL phenol red solution. Record the volume of 0.1 M hydrochloric acid required to change the colour of the indicator.

details.endpoint: colour change of the indicator (colours not stated)
details.titrantPreparation: 0.1 M HCl VS: dilute 100.0 mL of 1 M hydrochloric acid to 1000.0 mL with carbon dioxide-free water
details.indicatorPreparation: Phenol red solution: dissolve 0.1 g phenol red in a mixture of 2.82 mL 0.1 M sodium hydroxide and 20 mL ethanol (96 per cent), dilute to 100 mL with water
details.reference: BP 2023 Monograph for Sodium Lauryl Sulfate

tests.procedure: Dissolve 10.0 g in 100 mL water, add 100 mL ethanol (96 per cent). Extract with 3 quantities of 50 mL light petroleum (add sodium chloride if necessary to separate layers). Wash combined organic layers with 3 quantities of 50 mL water, dry over anhydrous sodium sulfate, filter, evaporate on a water-bath until the solvent has evaporated, heat the residue at 105 C for 30 min, cool, weigh the residue (maximum 0.4 g).

details.dissolvedIn: 100 mL water + 100 mL ethanol (96 per cent)
details.residueLimit: residue weighs a maximum of 0.4 g
details.calculation: not stated; limit 4.0 per cent corresponds to 0.4 g residue from 10.0 g (inferred)
details.reference: BP 2023 Monograph for Sodium Lauryl Sulfate
details.analystEntersFinalValue: Decision 2026-11-04: was Gravimetric in the transcription; now Measurement, the analyst enters the final value.

tests.procedure: Two determinations summed for the total: sodium chloride by argentometric titration, sodium sulfate gravimetrically as barium sulfate.

sodiumChloride.neutralisation: dilute nitric acid dropwise if necessary until neutral
sodiumChloride.addition: 5.0 mL of a 5.84 g/L sodium chloride solution
sodiumChloride.indicator: 0.1 mL of a 2 g/L solution of sodium fluoresceinate R
sodiumChloride.technique: stir vigorously to disperse silver chloride; endpoint first appearance of turbidity, colour from yellow green to orange through yellow
sodiumChloride.equivalenceFactor: 1 mL of 0.1 M silver nitrate is equivalent to 5.844 mg of NaCl

sodiumSulfate.step1: add 100 mL ethanol (96 per cent); heat just below boiling point for 2 h
sodiumSulfate.step2: filter hot through glass or porcelain filter; wash with 100 mL boiling ethanol (96 per cent)
sodiumSulfate.step3: dissolve precipitate by washing with 150 mL water into a beaker
sodiumSulfate.step4: add 10 mL dilute hydrochloric acid R, heat to boiling, add 25 mL of 120 g/L barium chloride R, stand overnight
sodiumSulfate.step5: collect precipitate by filtration or centrifugation; wash with water until last washing shows no opalescence with 0.1 M silver nitrate
sodiumSulfate.step6: dry the precipitate, ignite to constant mass at 500-600 C raising the temperature gradually; weigh as barium sulfate
sodiumSulfate.equivalenceFactor: 1 mg of barium sulfate is equivalent to 0.609 mg of Na2SO4

tests.procedure: Dissolve 1.15 g in water (warm if necessary), dilute to 1000.0 mL. To 20.0 mL of the solution add 15 mL methylene chloride and 10 mL dimidium bromide-sulfan blue mixed solution and mix. Titrate with 0.004 M benzethonium chloride, shaking vigorously and letting the layers separate before each addition, until the pink colour of the methylene chloride layer is completely discharged and a greyish-blue colour is obtained.

details.dissolution: in water, warming if necessary, dilute to 1000.0 mL
details.additions: 15 mL methylene chloride + 10 mL dimidium bromide-sulfan blue mixed solution
details.endpoint: pink colour of the methylene chloride layer completely discharged, greyish-blue colour obtained
details.equivalenceFactor: 1 mL of 0.004 M benzethonium chloride is equivalent to 1.154 mg of sodium alkyl sulfates
details.reference: BP 2023 Monograph for Sodium Lauryl Sulfate
details.analystEntersFinalValue: Decision 2026-11-04: was Titration in the transcription; now Measurement, the analyst enters the final value.

openQuestions.question: Sodium chloride and sodium sulfate: the STM gives two separate determinations (argentometric titration for NaCl, barium sulfate gravimetry for Na2SO4) but no formula for either result and no statement of how they are summed to the 8.0 % total; spec sheet technique says 'Thermogravimetry', which matches neither. The NaCl calculation must also account for the 5.0 mL of 5.84 g/L NaCl added (29.2 mg NaCl) and the blank; not stated. Confirm the calculation. One spec row kept with the stated limit.
openQuestions.source: Sodium Lauryl sulfate__Sodium Lauryl sulfate.txt:33; Specifications sheet:19

openQuestions.question: Assay: no calculation formula and no basis (as-is / dried) stated; 1 mL of 0.004 M benzethonium chloride = 1.154 mg sodium alkyl sulfates, sample 1.15 g in 1000 mL, 20.0 mL aliquot. As-is assumed for the row; confirm formula and basis.
openQuestions.source: Sodium Lauryl sulfate__Sodium Lauryl sulfate.txt:34; Specifications sheet:20

openQuestions.question: Preparation of 0.004 M benzethonium chloride (and its standardization), dimidium bromide-sulfan blue mixed solution, 0.1 M silver nitrate, 2 g/L sodium fluoresceinate, 5.84 g/L sodium chloride, dilute nitric acid, 500 g/L and 100 g/L sulfuric acid and 'dilute hydrochloric acid R' are used but not in the STM reagent-preparation list (only 'Sulfuric Acid, Dilute' 5.5 mL/100 mL is given).
Spec sheet reference is 'BP' with no year; the STM cites BP 2023 Monograph (most tests) and BP 2024 (Appearance, IR appendix). Row reference recorded as 'BP'; confirm the edition.
